title: MediaTimeline
description: koine's additive profile over an OpenTimelineIO (OTIO) Timeline — the canonical timeline / composition model a media authority (producer + authority for assets and timelines) serves to any media consumer, per KMI media-interchange.md §4 and decisions/ADR-0005. This schema deliberately does NOT re-specify OTIO: composition structure is OTIO's own, unmodified, and stays open (KMI adds no classes to OTIO's schema — §4.1). It checks only koine's additive layer (§4.2): every clip's media reference carries the KINP asset id at metadata.koine.asset, timing is OTIO RationalTime / TimeRange with no separate frame-rate field, and the optional asset-id ↔ resolved-path media map (delta I, §4.3). The asset-lineage graph (§3) and the analysis → knowledge bridge (§5) are KGP assertions that live OUTSIDE the timeline and are therefore out of scope here. The deprecated application/vnd.koine.edl+json form (§4.4) is not modelled: this schema validates the canonical form only, and rejects the legacy clip shape it maps from.

OTIO_SCHEMA.description: The root MUST be an OTIO Timeline (§4.1). Each item declares its own core-schema version, e.g. 'Timeline.1' — version negotiation is OTIO's mechanism, not KMI's.

global_start_time.description: Optional record start (timecode origin). Its rate is carried by the RationalTime itself.

tracks.description: OTIO's Stack of Tracks. Multitrack V/A conform (one video track over several audio tracks) needs nothing beyond Track.kind — it is a Stack of Tracks, not a KMI construct (§4.1).

not.$comment: The rate is carried by each RationalTime / TimeRange (§4.1). A document-level `fps` is the deprecated EDL shape (§4.4 mapping table), not the canonical one.

assetRef.description: A KINP asset id (identity.md §7.2): <namespace>:asset:<alg>-<hash>, content-addressed over the bytes. Namespaces in examples are the KINP §3.4 illustrative placeholders (analyzer / mediastore / worldsim). Distinct from provenance.schema.json#/$defs/assetId, which is the bare hash form used as a graph node reference in the canonical-graph export.

rationalTime.description: OTIO RationalTime — value + rate. The rate is carried by the time value itself; KMI defines no separate frame-rate field (§4.1).

timeRange.description: OTIO TimeRange — start_time + duration, each a RationalTime carrying its own rate. This is the canonical form of a clip's in/out (§4.4 maps the legacy in_ms/out_ms pair onto it).

stack.description: OTIO Stack — the timeline's track container, and also a nested sequence placed inside a Track.

track.description: OTIO Track. kind is 'Video' or 'Audio' per §4.1; a producer emitting another OTIO track kind is outside the profile KMI describes.

composable.description: Any OTIO composable child — Clip / Gap / Transition / nested Stack / Track. Only the classes koine constrains are branched on; every other OTIO class passes through untouched, because composition structure is OTIO's, unmodified (§4.1).

clip.description: OTIO Clip. koine's one obligation on it (§4.2a): the media it plays is addressed by KINP asset id, so a media reference MUST be present and MUST carry that id. The legacy per-clip in_ms / out_ms / timeline_ms fields (§4.4) are rejected — their canonical form is source_range plus position in the track's ordered children.

media_references.description: Alternate media references, where OTIO supports several per clip. These SHOULD be the assets linked media:variant_of (§3), each carrying its own metadata.koine.asset (§4.2a).

markers.description: OTIO Markers are a non-normative editorial mirror. Knowledge extracted from media is emitted as KGP assertions into the asset's source_world (§4.2c / §5), which is the normative form.

mediaReference.description: Any OTIO media reference (ExternalReference / MissingReference / ImageSequenceReference / GeneratorReference / …). OTIO addresses media by location; koine adds identity. The asset id is authoritative and the target_url advisory — a consumer that can fetch by id (§7) MUST prefer the id when the two disagree (§4.2a). A producer with no path to offer MUST still carry the id, on a MissingReference if necessary.

target_url.description: Location — advisory, and may be stale. Absent on a MissingReference.

koineMediaMetadata.description: koine's namespaced metadata on a media reference — the whole of what travels inside the timeline (§4.2a). Rides OTIO's own extension point, so a stock OTIO reader opens the document unchanged.

koineTimelineMetadata.description: Optional koine metadata on the Timeline itself (§4.2d). Nothing here is required for a timeline to be canonical; lineage (§3) and analysis (§5) are KGP assertions and are NOT carried here.

kmi_version.description: The KMI spec version the emitting side was built against.

mediaMap.description: The asset-id ↔ resolved-path media map (delta I, §4.3): one entry per referenced asset, mapping its KINP id to the path or URL the receiving side will resolve. Required somewhere alongside any serialization handed to a consumer that resolves media by path — an OTIO adapter's output, or a bundle serialization that carries the media instead. Without it every clip goes 'media offline' on the far side.

additionalProperties.description: The resolved path or URL for that asset on the receiving side.
